title: Adding a Subsystem Quiz
intro: 15 questions drawn from a pool of 30. You need 14 out of 15 to unlock the AltExtractor code. Most questions show a line of code and ask what it does, so read carefully. A few tries is normal.

questions.q: What is the FIRST step of the recipe for adding a new mechanism?
questions.correct: Add the device to the Driver Hub configuration
wrong: Write the button mapping in the TeleOp
Add a telemetry line for the new state
Call the new commands from an autonomous
questions.explain: Everything else depends on the configuration name: the subsystem uses it to find the hardware, Robot builds the subsystem, and the TeleOp uses Robot.

questions.q: How should the two extractor servos be set up in the Driver Hub configuration?
questions.correct: As Continuous Rotation Servo
wrong: As Servo
As goBILDA 5202/3/4 motor
As REV Touch Sensor
questions.explain: The code asks for a CRServo. A plain Servo is a positional servo, a different type, so hardwareMap.get(CRServo.class, ...) wouldn't find it.

questions.q: hardwareMap.get(CRServo.class, "extractor_left")  What must the text "extractor_left" match?
questions.correct: The device name in the robot configuration
wrong: The name of the AltExtractor.java file
The name of the field in Robot.java
The label printed on the servo's case
questions.explain: hardwareMap is the robot's phone book. It looks the device up by the exact name typed into the Driver Hub configuration.

questions.q: A CR servo is given setPower(1.0). What does it do?
questions.correct: Spins continuously at full speed
wrong: Moves to one end of its travel and holds
Moves to its middle position and stops
Spins one full turn and then stops
questions.explain: A continuous-rotation servo works like a small motor: setPower sets its speed and direction. A positional servo would use setPosition to go to a place.

questions.q: private static final double RUN_POWER = 1.0;  What does final mean here?
questions.correct: The value can't change while the program runs
wrong: It is the last constant in the class
Only the TeleOp is allowed to read it
The servos run it at the end of a match
questions.explain: final means once it is set it never changes. Together with static (one shared copy), that makes it a constant.

questions.q: private boolean running = false;  What does this field remember?
questions.correct: Whether the driver wants the wheels spinning
wrong: Whether the servos are turning this instant
How many pollen the wheels have pulled in
Whether D-pad down is pressed this loop
questions.explain: running is the subsystem's state: what we WANT. update() reads it every loop and makes the servos match.

questions.q: Why are the servo fields declared private final CRServo left;?
questions.correct: Only this class touches them, and they're set once
wrong: So the TeleOp can spin each servo directly
So a new servo can replace one mid-match
Because Java requires every CRServo to be final
questions.explain: private keeps everyone else out (they must use the commands), and final means the constructor sets them once and they never change.

questions.q: Why is there ONE AltExtractor subsystem for two servos, instead of one subsystem per servo?
questions.correct: The two wheels always work together as one mechanism
wrong: A subsystem may only hold one type of device
Robot.java can only add one new subsystem
Two subsystems would need two different buttons
questions.explain: A subsystem is a mechanism, not a single device. Both wheels start and stop together, so one subsystem owns both.

questions.q: right.setDirection(DcMotorSimple.Direction.REVERSE);  Why is this line here?
questions.correct: The servos are mirror-mounted, so one must spin backward
wrong: So the right wheel spins twice as fast
So the extractor runs backward when it's off
Because right-side servos are always wired backward
questions.explain: Mirror-mounted servos spin opposite ways for the same signal as seen from the robot. Reversing one makes positive power mean 'pull in' for both.

questions.q: If you left out the REVERSE line, what would mirror-mounted wheels do with the same power?
questions.correct: One pulls pollen in while the other pushes it out
wrong: Both pull pollen in, just a bit slower
The code would stop compiling
Neither servo would turn at all
questions.explain: Without the reverse, the two wheels fight each other. Fixing the direction once in the constructor means the rest of the code never has to think about it.

questions.q: catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { foundLeft = null; foundRight = null; }  When does this run?
questions.correct: When a servo name is missing from the configuration
wrong: When a servo spins the wrong direction
When the driver presses two buttons together
When a power value is bigger than 1.0
questions.explain: hardwareMap.get throws IllegalArgumentException if no device has that name. Catching it lets the robot run without the extractor instead of crashing at INIT.

questions.q: Why does the catch set BOTH servos to null, even if only the right one was missing?
questions.correct: So the extractor is either fully there or fully off
wrong: Java requires every variable in a try to be reset
So the left servo spins faster on its own
Because null makes the servos stop at INIT
questions.explain: One wheel spinning alone would push pollen sideways. hasExtractor() checks both, so a half-configured extractor safely does nothing.

questions.q: In the simulator (no extractor servos), what happens when this code runs?
questions.correct: It runs; telemetry shows ON/OFF and nothing moves
wrong: The OpMode crashes at INIT with an error
The intake roller spins in their place
The code won't compile in the simulator
questions.explain: The try/catch finds no servos and stores null, hasExtractor() is false, and update() returns early. The state still flips, so telemetry still changes.

questions.q: left.setPower(0.0); right.setPower(0.0);  Why are these in the constructor?
questions.correct: So nothing spins when INIT runs
wrong: To calibrate the servos' zero position
To turn on the servos' brake mode
To start the extractor running at INIT
questions.explain: Starting safe is part of every constructor in the recipe: nothing moves until a driver asks for it.

questions.q: public void toggle() { running = !running; }  What does it do?
questions.correct: Flips running from true to false, or false to true
wrong: Sets running to false every time
Spins the servos for one loop only
Reverses the direction of both servos
questions.explain: ! means 'not'. If running was true it becomes false, and the other way around.

questions.q: Why don't toggle(), on() and off() call setPower themselves?
questions.correct: Commands only change state; update() moves the hardware
wrong: CR servos can't be set from public methods
setPower only works inside the constructor
Two methods can't use the same servo in Java
questions.explain: Every subsystem in this course works this way: commands change the state, and update(), called every loop, makes the hardware match.

questions.q: Why does AltExtractor have on() and off() as well as toggle()?
questions.correct: Autos need to ask for an exact state, not a flip
wrong: toggle() doesn't work inside an autonomous
on() spins the wheels faster than toggle()
Every subsystem must have exactly three commands
questions.explain: A flip depends on what the state was. An auto should say exactly what it wants: on() means on, no matter what.

questions.q: double power = running ? RUN_POWER : 0.0;  What does this line do?
questions.correct: power is RUN_POWER if running, otherwise 0.0
wrong: power is 0.0 if running, otherwise RUN_POWER
running is set to the value of RUN_POWER
power is RUN_POWER plus 0.0 when running
questions.explain: The ternary operator: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. A one-line if/else that gives back a value.

questions.q: if (!hasExtractor()) { return; }  Why is this at the top of update()?
questions.correct: To skip the servos on a robot that doesn't have them
wrong: To stop the wheels while the button is up
To make update() run only once per match
To reset running back to false each loop
questions.explain: On a robot without the servos, left and right are null. Calling setPower on null would crash, so update() returns early.

questions.q: public class AltExtractor implements Subsystem  What does implements Subsystem promise?
questions.correct: The class has an update() the scheduler can call
wrong: The class is a child of the Robot class
The class gets its own Driver Hub button
The class can only control one servo
questions.explain: Subsystem is an interface with update(). Robot keeps a list of Subsystems and calls update() on each one every loop.

questions.q: You forget subsystems.add(altExtractor); in Robot.java. What happens?
questions.correct: It compiles, but the servos never move
wrong: It won't compile at all
The servos run nonstop from INIT
The robot crashes when INIT runs
questions.explain: The state still flips and telemetry still changes, but nobody calls update(), so no power is ever sent. The sneakiest mistake in the recipe.

questions.q: public final AltExtractor altExtractor; is in Robot.java, but you forget altExtractor = new AltExtractor(hardwareMap);. What happens?
questions.correct: Compile error: the final field is never given a value
wrong: It compiles, and the extractor does nothing
Java builds a default extractor for you
Only the telemetry line stops working
questions.explain: A final field must be assigned in the constructor. Java refuses to compile a final field that might never get a value.

questions.q: boolean pressedDown = gamepad1.dpad_down && !previousDpadDown;  When is pressedDown true?
questions.correct: Only on the first loop the button is down
wrong: Every loop while the button is held
Only on the loop the button is let go
Whenever the extractor is already on
questions.explain: It's true when the button is down now AND wasn't down last loop: the moment it's pressed. That's edge detection.

questions.q: You forget the line previousDpadDown = gamepad1.dpad_down;. What happens when the driver holds D-pad down?
questions.correct: It flips on and off every loop
wrong: It can never be turned on
The code won't compile without it
It turns on but never off
questions.explain: previousDpadDown stays false forever, so pressedDown is true every loop the button is held, and toggle() runs about 50 times a second.

questions.q: Why does tap-to-toggle need edge detection when the Extractor Arm's D-pad down didn't?
questions.correct: A toggle flips each time; deploy always meant the same
wrong: D-pad down is noisier than the other buttons
CR servos need it, but positional servos don't
Edge detection makes the servos spin faster
questions.explain: Saying 'deploy' 10 times in a row changes nothing. Saying 'flip' 10 times in a row changes it 10 times.

questions.q: Someone moves private boolean previousDpadDown = false; inside the while loop. What happens?
questions.correct: It restarts as false each loop, so holding keeps flipping
wrong: Nothing changes; it works exactly the same
The extractor can never be turned on
Compile error: no variables inside loops
questions.explain: A variable declared inside the loop is created fresh every loop and forgets the last one. Memory between loops has to be a field.

questions.q: The extractor starts OFF and the driver taps D-pad down three times. What is it now?
questions.correct: ON
wrong: OFF
ON, at a third of full power
Running backward
questions.explain: Each tap flips it once: off to on, on to off, off to on.

questions.q: An auto calls robot.altExtractor.on(); then waits in a loop that never calls robot.update(). What happens?
questions.correct: The wheels never start, because update() sends the power
wrong: They spin, since on() already set the power
They spin for one loop and then stop
The auto refuses to compile
questions.explain: on() only changes the state. The power reaches the servos in update(), so any waiting in an auto must keep calling robot.update().

questions.q: Telemetry says 'Alt extractor: ON' but the real robot's wheels don't move. Most likely cause?
questions.correct: A configuration name or servo type doesn't match
wrong: running is false even though it says ON
The edge detection is written backwards
RUN_POWER is too big for a CR servo
questions.explain: If either servo isn't found, the try/catch sets both to null and update() quietly does nothing, while the state and telemetry still change.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a team add both this lesson's code and the Extractor Arm code?
questions.correct: Both use D-pad down, so one tap runs two mechanisms
wrong: A Robot can't hold two extractor subsystems
Java forbids two classes named like Extractor
The simulator only allows one front servo
questions.explain: They are alternative designs for the same job. A robot has one or the other, so add only the one your robot actually has.
